newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco unit chooses Voisey's Bay smelter site.
newsitem.headline: Inco unit chooses Voisey's Bay smelter site.

text.p: Inco Ltd unit Voisey's Bay Nickel Co Ltd said on Friday it selected Argentia, Newfoundland, as the proposed site of the smelter-refinery complex that will process the nickel and cobalt concentrate produced at the Voisey's Bay base metals property.
The site is at the north side of the former U.S. Naval Base at Argentia, about 130 kilometers west of St. John's.

It concluded a three-month site evaluation process that evaluated all possible sites in the province. Argentia offers advantages in engineering and economics, particularly related to the costs of site preparation, the company said.
"Voisey's Bay Nickel Co will move forward to complete its due diligence on the site given that there are a number of legal and other issues that must be resolved," Voisey's Bay Nickel Co said.

The company plans to build the complex as soon as possible. But environmental assessment and permitting of the proposed complex must be completed. The company said it expected to register the project for environmental review in the coming weeks to allow enough time to obtain environmental permits and to have the complex operational to begin smelting nickel and cobalt concentrate in the year 2000.
The company is moving forward with plans for the mine/mill project at Voisey's Bay.

Early in 1997 a procurement and operations office will be established in Happy Valley-Goose Bay to support ongoing exploration activities in Labrador and to coordinate logistics during the construction and operations phase of the mine/mill.
